housing: Babergh is a rural district in south Suffolk, with the market towns of Sudbury and Hadleigh and many villages in the Stour valley and on the Shotley peninsula. It has a high share of listed and timber-framed buildings, especially in Lavenham, Long Melford and Hadleigh. Homes are mostly owner-occupied; rented homes range from terraces and flats in Sudbury to village cottages, and new estates have been built near Ipswich and Sudbury.
checkinTips: Timber-framed and listed cottages: photograph exposed beams, lime plaster walls and any cracks, and do not record repairs that would need listed building consent as tenant faults.
Thatched roofs in villages: photograph the visible thatch, the ridge and any signs of birds or wear, and note fire safety equipment.
Rural homes off mains gas: photograph oil tanks and the gauge level, and the access cover of any septic tank or treatment plant.
Woodburners and open fires common in cottages: photograph the stove glass, the hearth and the date on the last sweep certificate.
Older solid-walled homes: photograph window reveals, the bottom of walls and behind furniture for damp and mould.
tenantHelp: Tenants in Babergh can contact Babergh District Council’s private sector housing team (shared with Mid Suffolk) about disrepair, damp or unsafe conditions in a rented home.
